facts.text: The peaceful dove is a small pigeon found across Australia and New Guinea.
facts.quote: The peaceful dove (Geopelia placida) is a pigeon native to Australia and New Guinea.

facts.text: It has a pink-grey breast with chequered grey-brown wings.
facts.quote: The peaceful dove has a pink-grey breast with chequered grey-brown wings.
Calls of the peaceful dove are high-pitched "doodle-doo", "co-co-coo" and "croorrr!".

facts.text: The peaceful dove feeds off the ground and is commonly seen in streets and gardens.
facts.quote: They feed off the ground and are found commonly in streets and gardens.

facts.text: When not feeding on the ground, it can be found roosting in trees.
facts.quote: When not found on the ground feeding, they can be found in trees roosting.

facts.text: Its wings make a flushing 'frrr' noise when the birds are in flight.
facts.quote: The wings make a flushing "frrr" noise when the birds are in flight.

facts.text: Two white eggs are laid in nests built on horizontal branches of trees.
facts.quote: Nests are built on horizontal branches of trees. Two white eggs are laid.

facts.text: Peaceful doves become very aggressive to other birds when breeding.
facts.quote: The doves are very aggressive to other birds when breeding.

facts.text: Its range is shrinking because of competition with the introduced spotted turtle dove.
facts.quote: Unfortunately, the doves' range is reducing due to competition with the introduced spotted turtle dove.
